heard: Space Shuttle Atlantis lost over 700 thermal tiles during flight. On December 2, 1988, ablative insulating material from the right solid rocket booster struck the orbiter. 85 seconds into ascent, severe debris tore into the ship's vulnerable belly. Using the Canadarm, the crew inspected the heavy damage and grainy images were sent to mission control. Engineers dismissed the footage as mere lights and shadows, leaving Commander Robert Hoot Gibson convinced they would die. Atlantis survived fiery reentry because a missing tile sat squarely over a thick aluminum antenna plate. Over 700 thermal tiles were missing when space shuttle Atlantis finally returned to Earth.
